section_summary.extract_value: This general discussion section summarizes findings from two studies, emphasizing that Self-Competence is distinct from Self-Liking and the RSES due to its weaker association with self-deceptive enhancement. It highlights that self-competence correlates with emotional stability, task focus, responsibility, intelligence (fluid and crystallized IQ), and creativity, suggesting a more adaptive personality profile. The section also critiques the common reliance on the RSES for self-esteem measurement, advocating for the inclusion of self-competence assessment to provide a more complete understanding of self-evaluation.
